title: Cobalt- and platinum-free MTJ using iron shape anisotropy
idea: Inverts 'perpendicular MRAM needs Co, Pt, Ir, Ru and Ta': make tall Fe-B pillar free layers whose perpendicular anisotropy comes from shape (height > diameter) on an Fe/MgO interface, and pin the reference layer with a thick iron-nitride (Fe16N2) hard magnet instead of a Co/Pt synthetic antiferromagnet.
why: Nonvolatile with effectively unlimited endurance, so zero refresh; removes platinum-group metals and DRC cobalt from MRAM stacks.

title: CVD diamond heat spreaders keep hot-ambient DRAM twenty degrees cooler
idea: Magnify thermal conductivity ~5x over copper: bond a polycrystalline CVD diamond lid (grown from methane and hydrogen) to the memory die, so a 125 C ambient gives a ~105 C junction.
why: Every 10 C halves the needed refresh rate, so refresh energy and bandwidth loss fall ~4x (fact 3). Carbon is abundant and the lid is stable at 125 C indefinitely.

title: Lanmodulin-style protein splits hafnium from zirconium cheaply
idea: Lanmodulin binds rare earths about a billion times more tightly than calcium. Use directed evolution to engineer an EF-hand-like metal-binding protein that tells Hf4+ from Zr4+ by their tiny hydration and radius difference, then immobilize it on agarose columns to separate the two from US zircon-sand leachate in water at room temperature.
why: Hf/Zr separation now uses MIBK/thiocyanate solvent extraction and depends on nuclear-Zr output; a protein column could make US hafnium for high-k and HZO a primary product.

title: Unbundle hafnium from nuclear zirconium with a U.S. separation hub
idea: Periodic-table walk, Hf (72): hafnium exists only as a by-product of nuclear-grade Zr purification, so fund a Hf/Zr solvent-extraction plant fed by Florida-Georgia-Virginia heavy-mineral-sand zircon, with chipmaker offtake contracts and a strategic reserve.
why: Decouples high-k/HZO supply (~70-80 t/yr world) from reactor demand; ~2-3x supply resilience.

title: Vacuum-sealed bag: FPGA CXL card compresses memory inline
idea: Stimulus 'vacuum storage bag' (same clothes, a third of the space) -> a 10-person team builds an FPGA CXL memory expander that compresses cache lines inline (LZ4/base-delta hybrid with hardware page metadata), presenting 2-3x more logical capacity than physical DRAM.
why: Does DRAM's job with about half the bits for compressible (mostly cold) data, multiplying scarce DRAM supply per card.

title: Zuse Z1 mechanical memory shrunk to buckled silicon-carbide nanobeams
idea: Revive Konrad Zuse's 1938 sheet-metal mechanical memory as NEMS: a SiC nanobeam pre-buckled by residual stress snaps between up and down states under electrostatic pull and is read capacitively without switching. Because the state is mechanical geometry, no charge can leak away.
why: Zero leakage means no refresh (fact 3); uses only Si, C and N (no Hf, W or Ta); tolerates heat and radiation; claims nonvolatile working memory with ~10 ns switching, with endurance of 1e12+ cycles as the honest risk.

title: One zinc-oxide film serves as channel, wordline and electrode via hydrogen
idea: ZnO conductivity spans ~1e-6 to 1e3 S/cm depending on hydrogen donors; deposit one ZnO film per tier and convert wordline/electrode regions into degenerate conductor with self-aligned H-plasma through the slit, leaving the masked channel semiconducting.
why: Each tier needs 2 depositions (ZnO + Al2O3) instead of ~4, cutting tier cost ~40% so 100+ tiers fit the same budget (~10x density) with no W, Mo, In or Ga. Hydrogen diffusion stability is the risk.

title: Thermal-expansion valves cut idle purge-gas flows automatically
idea: TRIZ #37 Thermal expansion: fit tool gas lines with passive bimetal or shape-memory valves keyed to chamber-wall or heater temperature. When a chamber idles and cools, the valve throttles He, N2 and H2 purge to a trickle, and it reopens as the heaters ramp, with no software change or recipe requalification.
why: Idle purge is often 20-40% of process-gas use, so this cuts He and N2 consumption and the ASU energy behind it by a similar share.

title: Liquid-nitrogen-cooled DRAM pools shrink capacitors fivefold
idea: Box [1 fF stub cap, AR ~15:1 | Si access at 77 K | low-noise voltage SA | LN2-immersion rack shared over CXL | Si | standard]: at 77 K, subthreshold and junction leakage fall by >1e6, so retention exceeds hours and 1 fF suffices; cooling uses LN2 from air separation, which needs no helium (unlike sub-20 K cryogenics).
why: Capacitor wall, refresh and materials: ~5x less capacitor stack, near-zero refresh, and ~5x lower Cu wire resistance; the cryocooler overhead means it pays off only for dense pooled racks.

title: DNA origami places capacitor sites without EUV
idea: Inverts 'arrays must be patterned by light': DNA origami tiles made by bacterial fermentation self-assemble onto coarse pre-patterned landing pads and carry metal-oxide nanoparticle hardmask dots at 10-15 nm pitch that define capacitor and contact positions; the DNA is burned off after pattern transfer.
why: Replaces several of DRAM's 5-7 EUV layers (single-supplier tool, tin plasma source) with biologically manufactured patterning; capital per patterned layer down ~10x.

title: Myelinated printed bitlines: foamed low-k wrap for fast foil memory
idea: Myelin wraps an axon in low-capacitance lipid layers to speed conduction. Print bitlines as thick copper traces wrapped in a roll-to-roll foamed polyimide sheath (k~1.5), halving line capacitance so printed oxide-TFT arrays reach ~50-100 ns access over cm-long lines.
why: Brings printed, abundant-material memory toward DRAM-class latency, and the lower C also lowers CV2 energy per access.

title: Bronze-age metallurgist: zinc-tin oxide replaces gallium and indium
idea: Persona: a Bronze Age smith who built a civilisation on tin and zinc. For oxide-semiconductor access transistors and gain cells, use ALD amorphous zinc-tin oxide (ZTO) instead of IGZO, hydrogen-gettered under an Al2O3 cap. Indium and gallium are removed entirely.
why: Gallium is ~98% Chinese and export-controlled. Indium is a concentrated byproduct. ZTO keeps the ultra-low off-current needed for refresh-free cells.

title: Embargo engineer swaps helium backside cooling for hydrogen
idea: Persona: a Soviet engineer under embargo, with no helium. Run the electrostatic-chuck backside gas on dry H2 at 5-15 Torr through flow-limited orifices, with H2 detectors. H2 conducts heat at ~0.18 W/m-K versus 0.15 for He. Requalify recipes, because the few sccm that leak into the chamber act like the H2 additions many etch and CVD recipes already use.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30%, offline): removes the largest recurring He use in DRAM etch and deposition fleets. Per-wafer He use could fall >80% at near-zero capex.

title: Cold-crucible skull melting grows CZ ingots without any quartz
idea: A crucible's only job is to hold 1414 C silicon without contaminating it, and the purest container for silicon is solid silicon. Use a segmented water-cooled copper crucible with induction heating so a frozen Si skull lines the wall, and pull 300 mm crystals from an electromagnetically confined melt.
why: Eliminates high-purity quartz crucibles (>80% Spruce Pine) and crucible-sourced oxygen that seeds junction-leakage defects; costs ~30-50% more melt energy lost to cooling water.

title: Graphene lacked a bandgap; MoS2 capacitorless gain cells grown on glass
idea: Graphene logic programs stalled because a zero bandgap gives no off-state. Monolayer MoS2 (1.8 eV, 0.7 nm) shows off-currents below 1e-18 A/um: grow it by MOCVD at <=450 C directly on display glass and build 2T gain cells where the read transistor's gate is the storage node.
why: Retention of seconds or more cuts refresh energy >100x; no capacitor, so no Hf/Zr and no deep etch; a monolayer uses ~3 mg MoS2 per m2, from diversified Mo supply.

title: Solar-megafab continuous Czochralski: five ingots per crucible for DRAM wafers
idea: Solar ingot pullers run continuous CZ, recharging granular polysilicon while pulling, so one crucible yields 5-8 ingots instead of one. Port CCZ with fluidized-bed granular feeders and in-situ melt-level control to 300 mm prime DRAM-grade ingots, using oxygen-transport models to keep interstitial oxygen uniform over the long campaign.
why: Cuts HPQ crucibles per wafer ~5x and puller energy per kg ~20-30%, directly offsetting the Spruce Pine risk.

title: Eliminate tungsten: molybdenum buried wordlines and contacts from U.S. ore
idea: Replace W buried wordlines, bitline contacts and periphery plugs with fluorine-free ALD/CVD molybdenum (MoO2Cl2 precursor) sourced from Colorado/Arizona primary and by-product Mo. Mo's shorter electron mean free path gives lower line resistance than W below ~15 nm, so the buried wordline can be recessed shallower, which also reduces GIDL.
why: Removes China's ~80% tungsten chokepoint and WF6 handling from one of DRAM's four core metals; ~10-20% lower wordline RC at 12 nm-class pitch; near-zero supply risk on that input.

title: Chromium orbital-Hall torque layer replaces platinum, tungsten and tantalum
idea: Periodic-table walk, Cr (24) and Ti (22): light 3d metals have large orbital Hall conductivity; a Cr or Ti line under a thin Ni orbital-to-spin converter switches the free layer by orbital torque, replacing the Pt/W/Ta heavy-metal write line of SOT memory.
why: Removes W, Pt and Ta from spin-orbit-torque memory; lower-resistivity write lines cut write energy ~2x.

title: Magnetite-core ceria abrasives recaptured and reused tenfold
idea: Worsen: use ceria abrasives once and send rare-earth-laden slurry to wastewater. Flip: make the abrasives as a thin ceria shell on magnetite cores, so spent slurry passes a magnetic separator and the abrasives are washed, reclassified and reused ~10 times.
why: Ce chokepoint and slurry cost: ceria demand falls ~90%.

title: MRAM minus platinum and cobalt: tau-MnAl junctions with voltage writes
idea: MRAM lost the DRAM-replacement race (toggle MRAM density, STT write current) and its stacks lean on Pt, Ir, Ru, Co and Ta. Build perpendicular junctions from L10 tau-MnAl (high anisotropy, low damping) free and fixed layers around an MgO barrier, written by voltage-controlled-anisotropy pulses instead of current.
why: Removes PGMs and cobalt; Mn and Al have several independent supply regions; nonvolatile so refresh is gone; VCMA writes ~1-10 fJ/bit versus ~100 fJ for STT.

title: Indium-free zinc-tin-oxide gain cell with back-gate lockout
idea: Inverts 'oxide-semiconductor cells need indium and gallium': a 2T gain cell of amorphous Zn-Sn-O whose write transistor has a back gate held at about -2 V in standby, pushing off-current toward 1e-23 A so retention exceeds the data's useful life (target >1 year at 85 C) and refresh is removed.
why: Zero refresh; no indium (China ~60%) or gallium (China ~98%); sputtered and stackable at <400 C over logic.

title: Mist-CVD humidifier grows indium-free zinc oxide channels
idea: Like an ultrasonic humidifier or a spray gun, nebulize aqueous zinc acetate with silicon or aluminum dopant precursors and carry the mist in air onto ~300 C wafers to grow amorphous Zn-Si-O channels for BEOL access transistors, using zinc smelted in Tennessee.
why: Gives a wide-gap (3.3 eV), low-leakage, indium- and gallium-free channel for stacked gain cells with no vacuum, no organometallics and ~1/10 the energy of sputter or ALD lines.

title: Kidney countercurrent membrane cascade recovers helium from tool exhaust
idea: The loop of Henle multiplies concentration with countercurrent flow across selective membranes. Put roll-to-roll-cast polymer membrane sheets (polyimide or PIM films) in a countercurrent cascade on etch and CVD exhaust, concentrating dilute helium stage by stage to >99.999% for reinjection.
why: Recovers 70-90% of fab helium while Qatar (~30% of supply) is offline, using printable films at a fraction of cryogenic recovery capital.

title: Murray's-law tapered conductors cut metal use in arrays and grids
idea: Blood vessels and leaf veins follow Murray's law (radius cubed conserved at branches), minimizing material for a given flow. Lay out power meshes, wordline straps and bitline tapers with Murray-style branching, thick near drivers and thin at tips, instead of uniform-width lines.
why: Gives the same IR drop with ~20-30% less metal volume and routing area, freeing periphery (49% of the die) and reducing W/Cu deposition and CMP.

title: Termite mound: ballroom-free fab with clean air only inside tools
idea: Stimulus 'termite mound' (passive ventilation conditions only the nursery chambers) -> seal each process tool in its own HEPA micro-environment, move wafers only in N2-purged pods on enclosed rails, downgrade the open fab to ISO 8 and dump tool heat into earth-coupled loops.
why: HVAC and makeup air are ~40-50% of fab energy; shrinking the ISO 5 volume by >90% could cut fab energy ~25% and humidification water.

title: Liberty-ship mini-fabs: identical DUV-only DRAM fabs from used tools
idea: Revive the WWII Liberty-ship approach: freeze one standardized no-EUV DRAM design and fab layout (10k wafers/month, second-hand ArF-immersion scanners, refurbished etch and deposition tools) and have the same crews replicate it quickly across many US states.
why: Capital intensity and time to capacity: no EUV, ~1/5 the capex of a leading-edge fab, built in 18 months; claims to raise the US share of bits from 1-2% to ~5%.

title: HiPIMS-grown VO2 Mott latches hold bits inside hysteresis windows
idea: Effect: the Mott insulator-metal transition has an electrically driven hysteresis window. High-power impulse magnetron sputtering supplies energetic ions so monoclinic VO2 (Cr-doped to move the transition above 85 C operating temperature) crystallizes at <=300 C. A VO2 element biased inside its window latches as a one-resistor static bit switched by ns pulses.
why: Removes capacitor, high-k and W from the cell; vanadium has U.S. sources (Utah, Arkansas) and the whole process is BEOL-compatible below 400 C.

title: Spacecraft thermal straps: gasless nanotube chucks remove helium backside cooling
idea: Spacecraft move heat across vacuum joints with compliant metallic and CNT interfaces. Grow a vertically aligned CNT or Cu-nanowire forest on the chuck surface (university CVD or electroplating) so electrostatic clamping alone gives >2000 W/m2-K contact conductance without backside gas, and test particle shedding.
why: Removes helium from etch and deposition chucks entirely (Qatar risk) and simplifies chuck gas hardware.

title: NASA's vacuum-channel transistor as a zero-leakage DRAM access switch
idea: NASA's nanoscale vacuum-channel transistor stalled because emitter tips eroded under continuous current. A DRAM access device conducts only nanoseconds per access, a duty cycle near 1e-6: form 50-100 nm sealed vacuum gaps with carbon or Mo tips on glass that connect a storage capacitor to the bitline by field emission only when the wordline gate field passes threshold.
why: Off-state current across a vacuum gap is essentially zero, so retention of hours and no refresh; no doped semiconductor or silicon wafer; materials are glass, carbon or Mo and SiO2.

title: Non-wetting nitride crucibles exploit molten silicon contact-angle physics
idea: Effect: molten Si wets and dissolves silica but beads up (contact angle >90 deg) on dense reaction-bonded Si3N4 or CVD-SiC. Make crucibles from nitrogen and metallurgical silicon with a renewable nitride release coat; the light nitrogen doping it adds is the same doping already used to strengthen CZ wafers.
why: Quartz chokepoint: crucible feedstock becomes N2 plus metallurgical Si, which the U.S. can produce; crucible could be reused 5-10 pulls instead of once.

title: Vacuum-gap storage capacitors with no dielectric material at all
idea: Ideal: a dielectric that costs nothing and never leaks. Closest: interdigitated vertical fin electrodes (TiN or doped Si) separated by a 4-6 nm sacrificial carbon layer that is ashed out through vent holes, leaving vacuum gaps held open by periodic oxide anchors; many fins in parallel recover capacitance.
why: Removes Hf/Zr high-k ALD and dielectric leakage (a refresh driver; vacuum tunneling at 1 V/5 nm is negligible); needs ~10x electrode area, so best for gain-cell/low-Cs designs.

title: Embedded-substrate failures fixed: memory tiers deposited inside glass package cores
idea: Embedded dies and passives in organic substrates failed because one bad buried part scrapped an expensive package. As processors move to glass-core substrates, deposit 2-4 oxide-TFT memory tiers on the glass core panel before build-up, test them with built-in self-test and redundancy repair at panel level, and bin packages by working capacity so a bad tier downgrades, never scraps.
why: Puts gigabytes of DRAM-class memory 1-3 mm under the processor, cutting data movement from 3-4 pJ/bit toward ~0.5 pJ/bit, with no silicon wafer, TSVs or HBM area tax; the glass core is already paid for.

title: Child says rust holds the magnet: hematite pins MRAM, not iridium
idea: Persona: a child notices that rusty nails still stick. Replace the IrMn antiferromagnetic pinning layer in MTJ stacks with an epitaxial alpha-Fe2O3 (hematite) or NiO film, deposited by reactive sputtering. Its exchange bias pins the reference layer.
why: Non-volatile MRAM without its scarcest element: world iridium supply is ~7 t/yr. The insulating pin layer also reduces shunting.

title: Spatial ALD with cold-trap recapture recycles hafnium and zirconium precursors
idea: Magnify precursor utilization from ~5% to ~80%: spatial ALD heads confine TEMAZ/TEMAH to millimetre gaps and exhaust into cold traps, and the condensate is re-distilled on site and returned to the bubbler.
why: Hafnium, zirconium and ruthenium precursors are costly and concentrated. Consumption per wafer falls ~15x, and abatement energy falls with it.

title: Substitute solar-grade handle wafers for prime CZ silicon substrates
idea: Grow a ~10 um prime epitaxial device layer on a porous-silicon release layer atop a reusable donor wafer, bond and split it onto a cheap solar-grade or recycled-silicon handle, then re-polish and reuse the donor 20+ times.
why: Cuts prime silicon, crucible quartz and polysilicon energy per DRAM wafer by ~10x; handles come from abundant solar supply chains already scaled to hundreds of GW.

title: Solar kerfless epitaxial wafers grown on reusable porous-silicon seeds
idea: Adapted from the solar industry's kerfless wafer process: epitaxial silicon is grown from trichlorosilane on a porous-silicon release layer atop a reusable template, then detached. Grow 150-300 um, 300 mm DRAM substrate wafers directly from gas and reuse each template 20-50 times.
why: Skips Czochralski pulling, quartz crucibles, argon-hungry pullers and wire sawing. Substrate energy roughly halves, and crucible plus polysilicon intensity per wafer falls >3x.

title: Sourdough-starter wafers: one CZ seed donates twenty transferred device layers
idea: As a baker keeps one starter alive and bakes off it, grow a 1-2 um epitaxial device layer on a porous-silicon release layer of a premium CZ seed wafer, bond it to a cheap kerfless direct-cast or reclaimed handle wafer, split along the porous layer (ELTRAN-style), re-polish the seed and repeat 10-20 times. Buried wordlines and access transistors live in the transferred epi film.
why: DRAM transistors use only the top few hundred nm of silicon; seed reuse cuts premium CZ crystal, HPQ crucible and argon per wafer by ~5-10x.

title: Reusable seed wafer: peel micron DRAM films, skip new ingots
idea: Inverts 'every die consumes a slab of crucible-grown silicon': grow a 5-8 um epitaxial device layer on a porous-silicon release layer on a seed wafer, bond it to a cheap carrier (reclaimed or low-grade wafer), cleave at the porous layer, re-polish the seed and repeat 30-50 times. The DRAM array and periphery only need the top few microns of perfect crystal.
why: Cuts Cz ingot, high-purity quartz crucible and polysilicon demand per bit ~20-40x (attacks the Spruce Pine >80% chokepoint) plus ingot-growth energy.

title: Thin device-layer transfer reuses one premium silicon donor many times
idea: Worsen: grow, polish and use up a full 775 um 11N CZ wafer for a DRAM whose active region is under 5 um deep. Flip: grow a ~10 um epitaxial device layer on a porous-silicon release layer, bond it to a cheap upgraded-metallurgical or recycled-silicon handle, split it off, and re-grow epi on the donor 10+ times.
why: Polysilicon energy, quartz crucibles and CZ pulling per bit: ~10x less premium silicon per wafer, and the handle can use lower-grade feedstock.

title: Kerfless solar trick: epi DRAM wafers lifted off reusable porous-silicon parents
idea: Kerfless solar firms grow epitaxial wafers on porous-silicon release layers and reuse the parent wafer dozens of times. For DRAM, grow a 20-50 um device-grade epi layer on double-porous Si, bond it to a cheap carrier (UMG or recycled Si), split it off, and repolish the CZ parent for 10-20 reuses.
why: Only the top few um of a DRAM wafer are active: cuts prime CZ silicon, HPQ crucibles and polysilicon per bit ~10x.

title: Molten-salt electro-epitaxy grows wafers without Siemens or Czochralski
idea: Imposed scarcity: no polysilicon reactor and no crystal puller. Electrodeposit 300-700 um of single-crystal silicon from a KF-KCl-K2SiF6 molten salt at ~750 C onto a seed wafer capped with a weak porous-silicon release layer, then peel off the grown wafer and reuse the seed.
why: Collapses polysilicon (Siemens ~60-100 kWh/kg) and CZ (HPQ crucible, argon) into one low-temperature electrochemical step; a possible ~3x energy cut per wafer and zero crucible use.

title: LNG regasification cold runs refresh-free cryogenic memory racks
idea: Imposed scarcity: no power budget for refresh. Site memory-heavy data halls at LNG import terminals and use the ~-160 C cold released during regasification, through a nitrogen loop, to hold DRAM at ~100-120 K, where access-transistor leakage collapses and refresh intervals can stretch >1000x.
why: Refresh (16-33% of idle DRAM power) and most cooling energy disappear using free waste cold, with no helium; higher carrier mobility at low temperature also trims access time.

title: Continuous-recharge Czochralski stretches one crucible across many ingots
idea: TRIZ #20 Continuity of useful action: grow 300 mm DRAM-grade crystal by continuous CZ. Granular polysilicon feeds through a weir-partitioned double crucible while a magnetic field (MCZ) holds oxygen and melt height constant, giving 5-10 ingots per crucible instead of 1-2.
why: Crucibles per wafer fall 3-5x, which eases the HPQ chokepoint. Flatter axial oxygen and dopant profiles add ~15% usable ingot length.

title: Continuous Czochralski stretches one quartz crucible across many 300mm ingots
idea: Time shift from one crucible per ingot (~150 h, then cracked on cooldown) to 600-1000 h of hot service. Granular FBR polysilicon is fed continuously through a weir into an outer melt ring while 5-8 ingots are pulled in sequence.
why: 5-8x fewer HPQ crucibles per DRAM wafer, plus flatter oxygen and dopant profiles. Proven in solar but not yet qualified for prime DRAM-grade 300 mm wafers.

title: Child asks why helium is allowed to float away
idea: Persona: a child asks 'why do you let the balloon go?' Put a cryo-sorption trap on each turbo-pump foreline and a small PSA/membrane purifier on each tool. Together they recover backside-leak and purge helium at >95% purity and refill a local manifold, closing the loop tool by tool.
why: Helium chokepoint: recovers 70-90% of the He consumed, with a payback of months at 2026 prices.

title: Direct-tunnel nitride-trap cell: seconds-long retention from silicon, nitrogen, oxygen
idea: Magnify retention from milliseconds to ~100 s at 125 C: store charge in deep silicon-nitride traps behind a 1.5-2 nm tunnel oxide, written by direct tunneling (no hot carriers) and read non-destructively through the transistor's threshold shift.
why: No capacitor, high-k or tungsten in the cell, and refresh is ~1000x rarer; low-field direct tunneling targets ~1e14 endurance.

title: Grain-roughened TiN electrodes let plain alumina replace hafnia capacitors
idea: Magnify electrode area ~2.5x by reviving 1990s hemispherical-grain roughening in TiN form (seeded nanocrystal nucleation inside the hole), so a robust Al2O3/TiO2 laminate (k ~20) stores the same charge as ZrO2/HfO2.
why: Alumina's wide bandgap and lack of phase transitions make 125 C/10-year TDDB and leakage easier to meet, and hafnium and zirconium leave the cell.

title: Po dies stacked without touching: inductive-coupled TSV-free HBM
idea: Po: 'stacked dies that never touch.' Extracted: replace thousands of copper TSVs with on-die spiral-coil inductive transceivers that couple data through 20-50 um thinned dies, and bring power in through edge-plated pads, so DRAM dies need no TSV keep-out zones and no via-reveal process.
why: HBM TSV tax (~3x wafer area per bit vs DDR5, yield down 20-30%): recovers most TSV area plus copper fill and reveal steps; coil arrays sit in top metal over the array.

title: Zero-vent fab: noble gases treated as leased capital, not consumables
idea: Inverts 'process gases are bought, used once and vented': a fab-wide exhaust spine with cryogenic fractional distillation and membranes recovers He, Ne, Kr, Xe and NF3 from every tool exhaust before abatement, repurifies to 6N and returns them to gas cabinets; the gas vendor keeps ownership and bills only for grams lost.
why: Targets >85% recovery of helium and neon (Qatar, Ukraine/Russia chokepoints), turning a supply shock into a small make-up stream; the lease model aligns the vendor with recovery.

title: Pharmacist's zinc and magnesia: all-zinc-oxide ferroelectric transistor
idea: Persona: a pharmacist looking at zinc ointment and milk of magnesia. Grow ferroelectric wurtzite Zn(1-x)Mg(x)O epitaxially on a ZnO channel, which is the same crystal family and nearly lattice-matched. The result is a FeFET with none of the amorphous interfacial dead layer that limits HfO2 FeFETs to ~1e5 cycles.
why: Non-volatile 1T cell made only of Zn, Mg and O at BEOL temperatures. The coherent interface aims at >1e10 cycles.

title: Brownout-tolerant fab: process excursions become BER bins
idea: Reverse the tie between power quality and yield: run non-critical tools straight on intermittent renewables without full UPS, let power-dip excursions degrade some wafers, and bin those wafers by raw BER up to 1%.
why: Cuts fab power-conditioning capex and lets fabs site on cheaper, cleaner grids.

title: Silicon holds itself: cold-crucible skull Czochralski growth
idea: Reverse container and content: melt silicon by induction inside a water-cooled segmented copper crucible so a frozen silicon skull forms the only wall the melt touches, then pull 300 mm ingots from the levitated-contact melt with a cusp magnetic field for oxygen-free, quartz-free growth.
why: Removes the high-purity quartz crucible (Spruce Pine >80% chokepoint) from DRAM wafer supply entirely; also drops interstitial oxygen, which improves retention-tail gettering control.

title: Zone-melting recrystallization stacks DRAM tiers without new wafers
idea: Revive MIT Lincoln Lab's 1980s zone-melting recrystallization: deposit amorphous silicon over a finished DRAM tier, melt it with a scanned line laser seeded through vias to form single-crystal islands, and build the next DUV-patterned tier on it, repeating for 8-16 tiers.
why: Density comes from tiers rather than EUV pitch (facts 2, 4), and no tier needs its own Czochralski wafer (quartz crucible) or bonding; claims 8x bits per wafer from 16 DUV tiers at 2x pitch.

title: Via-ROM for frozen AI weights: nothing to refresh
idea: Inverts 'working memory must be rewritable': store fixed model weights as present/absent or size-coded (2-bit) vias in a dense crosspoint read-only array using two custom mask layers on a mature node; changing the model re-spins only the via mask, and only activations use DRAM.
why: Zero refresh power with no capacitor, high-k or tungsten pillars; frees 50-80% of inference DRAM/HBM at 2-4 bits per F2.

title: Optane rebuilt from abundant elements: one-film sulfide self-selecting crosspoint
idea: 3D XPoint died on cost: roughly a dozen distinct films per deck (As-Ge-Se OTS selector, GST phase-change layer, carbon electrodes, W lines) made at tiny volume. Fix exactly that by collapsing selector plus storage into one As-free, Te-free sulfur-rich Sn-Al-S chalcogenide glass whose polarity-dependent threshold voltage is the bit (self-selecting memory, no melt-quench), between Mo lines, so a deck is three films.
why: Removes arsenic, germanium (China ~60%) and tellurium (copper-refining by-product) plus ~9 depositions per deck; no melting lifts endurance toward 1e10+ and cuts write energy; est. 40-50% lower cost per bit than Optane on cost and scarce-resource axes.

title: Dry-lubricant molybdenite monolayers as a domestic-supply gain-cell channel
idea: Molybdenite (MoS2) is mined in Colorado mainly for lubricants and steel. Adapt CVD monolayer MoS2 (1.8 eV gap, no dangling bonds) as the write transistor of a capacitor-free gain cell, where the 2D channel's tiny off-current lets the read transistor's own gate hold charge for seconds or longer.
why: Capacitor-free and indium-free, built on a US-mined element. Retention could cut refresh energy >100x (Fact 3).

title: Z-RAM without SOI wafers: floating bodies over silicon-on-nothing voids
idea: Innovative Silicon's Z-RAM died because it needed SOI wafers (two Cz wafers per substrate via bonding) and lost sense margin on bulk. Form local empty-space voids under the array by hydrogen-anneal surface migration of deep trench lattices (silicon-on-nothing), then partially refill each void with doped poly as a buried back-gate plate so every floating body has a strong back gate to hold stored holes.
why: Capacitorless ~4F2 cell drops the 60-75:1 TiN/ZrO2 pillar (no Zr/Hf, no high-AR fluorocarbon etch) and avoids SOI's 2x Cz silicon and quartz-crucible use per substrate; ~1.5x density and ~50% less crystal silicon per bit.

title: Architectural low-E glass zinc-tin-oxide for an indium-free gain cell
idea: Low-emissivity window coaters sputter zinc stannate (ZTO) over huge areas of glass every year. Adapt their target chemistry and rotary-sputter tooling to a two-transistor, zero-capacitor gain cell whose wide-bandgap ZTO write transistor leaks sub-fA, so the read transistor's gate holds the bit for seconds.
why: Removes the capacitor plus indium and gallium (heavily China-concentrated) from oxide gain cells. Zn and Sn have diversified supply, and the BEOL process stays below 400 C.

title: Substitute supercritical CO2 for ultrapure-water wet cleans
idea: Run post-etch residue and particle cleans in single-wafer supercritical CO2 chambers (100-200 bar, 40-60 C) with 1-5% amine/alcohol chelant co-solvent, recompressing and recycling >95% of the CO2 on-tool; no DI rinse and no spin dry.
why: Wet cleans plus rinses are ~40-50% of fab UPW; this module drops its water >20x and removes capillary collapse of high-AR capacitor and wordline features.

title: Potter fires a reusable silicon nitride crucible for twenty pulls
idea: Persona: a potter who reuses kiln furniture. Replace single-use fused-quartz crucibles with dense reaction-bonded Si3N4 crucibles that carry a renewable sprayed Si3N4/SiO2 release coat, each reused for 10-20 pulls. Dose oxygen into the melt on purpose from a small sacrificial silica rod instead of relying on crucible dissolution.
why: Cuts high-purity quartz use per wafer 10-20x and decouples oxygen control from crucible wear.

title: S-layer protein crystals template ten-nanometer charge-storage dot arrays
idea: Ideal: a nanopattern brewed in a fermenter. Closest: recrystallize bacterial S-layer proteins (2D lattices, 3-30 nm period, cheap fermentation) on a gate dielectric, use their pores to template ALD/electroless Ni or ZnO nanodots as isolated charge sites for a dense floating-dot volatile cell, then burn the protein away.
why: 100x: protein at ~$1/g covers ~1e4 m2 per gram; sub-15 nm periodic sites without litho enable dense multi-level cells on cheap tiers toward ~$0.1/GB. Trades thermal limits and domain defects.

title: Diamond-wire kerf recycled into Czochralski recharge feedstock
idea: Within $1M/24 months: bench-pilot recovery of silicon kerf from 300 mm wafering (30-40% of the ingot) using froth flotation to strip coolant and diamond, an HCl leach for Fe/Ni, and induction melting with slag refining into recharge rods that meet CZ spec.
why: Returns about a third of every ingot to feedstock, cutting polysilicon demand and Siemens energy per wafer by up to ~30%.

title: MgB2 persistor arrays: niobium-free cryogenic memory without liquid helium
idea: Revive the 1957 persistor (a persistent supercurrent loop) and Buck's cryotron in magnesium diboride (Tc 39 K): bits are clockwise or counterclockwise currents in MgB2 loops switched by thermal cryotron gates. The arrays run at 20-25 K on sealed pulse-tube coolers rather than liquid-helium baths.
why: Avoids consuming helium (Qatar outage) and the niobium chokepoint of SFQ memory (~85% from one Brazilian producer); zero-resistance loops need no refresh; claims 10-100x lower energy per access for cryogenic AI and quantum controllers.

title: Telephone-exchange Erlang trunking for memory: optical circuit-switched DRAM pools
idea: Revive Bell System Erlang traffic engineering and crossbar exchanges: size rack memory like phone trunks, to the 99.9th-percentile aggregate demand rather than each server's peak, and connect servers to pooled DRAM through MEMS optical circuit switches carrying CXL over optics.
why: Scarce-resource intensity: about 25-30% of cloud DRAM sits stranded, and Erlang provisioning cuts purchased DRAM 20-30% with no new fabs and no EUV.

title: Thermally reversible Diels-Alder adhesive lets HBM stacks be unstacked
idea: Worsen: lock HBM dies together with permanent underfill and Cu-Cu bonds, so one bad die scraps the whole 12-high stack. Flip: bond the core dies with a Diels-Alder polymer underlayer and low-melting Sn-Bi microbumps that release at ~150 C, so a failed die can be heated out and replaced and the stack rebonded.
why: HBM yield loss (20-30%) and the wafer-area tax: recovering 11 good dies per failed stack could lift effective HBM output ~15-25%.

title: Electroless nickel-boron electrodes coat 100:1 capacitor holes conformally
idea: Box [MIM cap with Ni-B electrodes | Si | voltage SA | standard | Si | autocatalytic electroless deposition after molecular Sn/Ag activation]: seed the hole walls, grow 3 nm Ni-B autocatalytically (self-limiting by bath depletion), then nitridize its surface with NH3 for a stable interface to the dielectric.
why: Replaces slow TiCl4/NH3 ALD TiN with a wet, room-temperature process that is conformal at any aspect ratio, needs no vacuum or rare gases, and uses broadly sourced Ni.

title: Helium-off etch: edge dies carry extra parity
idea: Rearrange reliability by location: run etch tools without helium backside gas, accept the resulting radial temperature/CD drift, and assign stronger ECC to edge-zone dies or rows (from a known radial map) so their ~1% raw BER is absorbed.
why: Eliminates most fab helium demand (Qatar ~30% offline) with no new tool; costs ~5% extra parity on outer-ring dies.

title: Tin-oxo dry resist converts itself into the etch hardmask
idea: Combine EUV photoresist and hardmask: vapor-deposited tin-oxo-cluster resist is exposed and dry-developed, then an in-situ O2/H2O plasma densifies the remaining pattern into SnO2 that serves directly as the etch hardmask, deleting fluorinated-PAG resist, spin-on carbon and SiON layers.
why: Drops PFAS-bearing photoacid generators and 2-3 film depositions per critical layer; dry develop cuts solvent waste ~5-10x; lower dose frees scarce EUV scanner time.

title: Plasma-deposited organosilicon resist converts to glass under exposure
idea: TRIZ #32 Color changes (exposure switches the film's chemistry): plasma-deposit a solvent-free methylsilane film whose exposed areas photo-oxidize into SiO2-like glass, then dry-develop the unexposed film in a Cl2 plasma.
why: Removes PFAS photoacid generators, spin solvents and developer water, and avoids tin-oxo EUV resists. Uses only Si, C, H, O and Cl.

title: Ninety-degree hydrothermal zinc-oxide nanowires form vertical gain-cell forests
idea: Crystal growth needs supersaturation, not vacuum: ZnO nanowires grow from zinc nitrate/HMTA solution at 90 C on seed dots placed at 20 nm pitch by DUV plus pitch division. Each wire is a 4F2 vertical gain-cell channel; repeat seeding to build 5 decks.
why: 400 nm2/cell per deck x 5 decks = ~10x density with near-zero capex and energy for channel growth; Zn is abundant. Hydrogen-donor background doping (turn-off) is the risk.

title: Cubic-zirconia skull melting: quartz-free cold-crucible Czochralski silicon
idea: Cubic zirconia is grown in a water-cooled, segmented copper 'cold crucible': RF induction melts the charge while a frozen skin of the same material forms the container. Apply it to silicon: hold an induction-heated melt in its own frozen silicon skull inside a slotted copper crucible, with electromagnetic confinement shaping the melt surface for Czochralski pulling of 300 mm ingots.
why: Eliminates the high-purity quartz crucible (Spruce Pine >80%) entirely and yields near-oxygen-free silicon, removing oxygen-precipitate defects that feed the junction-leakage retention tail; 100% HPQ removal if melt stability is solved.

title: Soviet cold-crucible skull melting for crucible-free Czochralski silicon
idea: Revive Soviet-era cold-crucible induction melting: hold the silicon melt in a water-cooled, segmented copper crucible where a frozen silicon skull forms the container, then pull Czochralski ingots from it, adding oxygen by gas doping for gettering.
why: Removes quartz crucibles (Spruce Pine) and their per-pull consumption entirely; copper and water are abundant; claims zero crucible spend, at the cost of ~2x melt energy.

title: Cold-crucible Czochralski: silicon melt levitated, no quartz contact
idea: Inverts 'silicon melt must sit in a high-purity quartz crucible': hold the melt in a water-cooled segmented copper crucible by induction, with a thin frozen silicon skull as the container, and pull the crystal from it; electromagnetic stirring sets interstitial oxygen.
why: Eliminates Spruce Pine HPQ crucibles (>80% share); lower oxygen also tightens the retention tail; the crucible becomes permanent capital, not a consumable.

title: Igloo: silicon skull crucible eliminates high-purity quartz crucibles
idea: Stimulus 'igloo' (a shelter built from the very material it keeps out) -> melt silicon in a water-cooled segmented copper cold crucible by RF induction so a frozen silicon skin forms the crucible wall; pull Cz-style 300 mm crystals from the skull melt and add controlled oxygen through a gas-phase SiO doser to keep gettering.
why: Removes the Spruce Pine high-purity-quartz crucible dependency (>80% concentration) and crucible contamination; higher RF energy is the trade-off, partly offset by continuous recharge.

title: Cold-crucible induction Czochralski growth with no quartz at all
idea: Box [standard 1T1C | Si access | voltage SA | standard | ingot pulled from a segmented water-cooled copper cold crucible with RF-levitated melt skull | magnetic CZ]: the melt touches only its own frozen Si skull, so no silica crucible and near-zero oxygen; nitrogen co-doping at 1e14-1e15 cm-3 replaces oxygen precipitates for intrinsic gettering.
why: Eliminates Spruce Pine HPQ crucible dependence outright and removes thermal-donor variability; RF energy rises ~20-30% per pull, but each $1-3k crucible and its supply risk disappear.

title: No-till farmer grows silicon without any quartz crucible
idea: Persona: a no-till farmer skips the plow, so skip the crucible. Run Czochralski growth from a cold, segmented, water-cooled copper crucible. Induction fields push the melt off the walls, so a frozen silicon skull is the only wall the melt touches. Add nitrogen co-doping to make up for the wafer strength normally supplied by oxygen.
why: Removes Spruce Pine high-purity quartz (>80% share) from DRAM wafer supply. Lower interstitial oxygen means fewer precipitate defects in the retention tail.

title: Containerless space-furnace logic: cold-crucible induction Czochralski for 300 mm
idea: Space crystal growers avoid containers altogether. On Earth, a segmented water-cooled copper cold crucible with induction heating makes silicon hold itself inside a frozen Si skull, so the melt never touches quartz. Controlled O2/Ar ambient or SiO dosing restores the oxygen needed for intrinsic gettering, and cusp magnetic fields steady the melt.
why: Eliminates quartz crucibles entirely (the HPQ chokepoint) and lowers metal contamination, at roughly 2x melt power, which is small next to crucible scarcity risk.

title: Quartz-free crystal pulling: cold-crucible Czochralski from failed electromagnetic casting
idea: Electromagnetic casting held molten silicon in a water-cooled segmented copper crucible by induction, with no quartz, but died because it only made multicrystalline solar ingots. Combine that cold crucible with seed pulling and a cusp magnetic field so 300 mm dislocation-free crystals grow with zero quartz contact, and add nitrogen doping for gettering since the crystal is now oxygen-poor.
why: Removes the Spruce Pine high-purity quartz crucible (>80% single site) from DRAM wafer supply; oxygen-free crystals avoid thermal donors; melt power rises ~30% but one consumable chokepoint disappears.

title: Cold-crucible induction skull melting gives quartz-free Czochralski silicon
idea: Effect: eddy-current induction heats silicon inside a segmented, water-cooled copper crucible while the Lorentz force pushes the melt off the wall, so molten Si rests on its own frozen Si skull and never touches fused quartz; add a cusp magnetic field to damp convection while pulling 300 mm crystals.
why: High-purity quartz crucibles (Spruce Pine >80%): removes about one crucible per ingot and most oxygen contamination, at roughly +30-50% melt energy.

title: Crucible-free 300 mm silicon via cold-crucible induction skull melting
idea: Ideal: a crystal grown from a melt that touches nothing. Closest: pull 300 mm Cz crystals from a water-cooled segmented copper cold crucible where induction heats and partly levitates the melt and a frozen silicon skull is the container; interstitial oxygen for gettering is dosed via a controlled O2/Ar ambient instead of dissolving quartz.
why: Removes the Spruce Pine (>80%) high-purity quartz crucible chokepoint and gives tighter oxygen control; costs ~1.5-2x melt energy.

title: Eliminate silicon interposers: glass-core panel interposers put DRAM 2 mm away
idea: Mount memory dies on glass-core panel interposers (abundant borosilicate, 2 um lines, through-glass vias) within ~2 mm of the processor, driving unterminated low-swing links in place of CoWoS silicon interposers and ABF substrates.
why: Link energy falls to ~0.3-0.5 pJ/bit versus 10-20 for DDR5 (>10x), escaping the silicon-interposer and ABF chokepoints.

title: Cryogenic-etch silicon mold builds capacitor holes without fluorocarbon gases
idea: Extreme-cold etching (-110 C SF6/O2 DRIE) carves 50:1+ holes in silicon behind an SiOxFy passivation that evaporates on warm-up, with no C4F6/C4F8 polymer. Replace the oxide capacitor mold with amorphous Si, etch the holes cryogenically in a university ICP tool, deposit TiN/ZrO2/TiN, then strip the Si mold with XeF2 vapor behind a SiN support lattice.
why: Removes PFAS-class, high-GWP fluorocarbon gases from DRAM's highest-AR step (fact 1) and uses faster, cheaper Si etching.

title: Catalytic wet-etched silicon molds for 115:1 capacitors
idea: Imposed scarcity: no fluorocarbon plasma and no high-aspect-ratio etch tool. Deposit a sacrificial silicon mold above a nitride barrier, pattern a graphene or Pt catalyst mesh, and let catalyst-assisted chemical etching in HF/H2O2 sink vertical holes beyond 100:1; line them with TiN/ZAZ, then dissolve the silicon mold in TMAH.
why: Reaches the AR~115 capacitor charge wall with no PFC gases (high GWP, PFAS rules) and no $5M+ etcher; holes stay straight because the catalyst sinks chemically rather than relying on ion flux.

title: Dairy-grade plumbing: electropolished stainless and polyolefins replace fluoropolymers
idea: Dairies and breweries run clean-in-place 316L electropolished stainless with passivated chromium-oxide skins; rebuild fab solvent, gas and ultrapure-water distribution from electropolished, ozone-passivated stainless and reserve high-purity polypropylene and polyethylene for acids, removing PFA and PVDF wetted parts.
why: Fluoropolymer piping, valves and tanks are the bulk of a fab's PFAS inventory and a supply risk as PFAS rules tighten; stainless and polyolefins are abundant, domestic and recyclable.

title: Refinery stripping of chamber shields recovers tungsten and hafnium
idea: Gold refiners strip plated scrap electrochemically; instead of bead-blasting deposits off PVD, CVD and ALD chamber shields into landfill, strip them in selective anodic baths that redissolve W, Mo, Hf, Zr, Ru and Ta, then precipitate and calcine each metal as a pure salt for precursor makers.
why: Chamber kits accumulate a large share of deposited metal (PVD target utilization is only ~30-40%); recovery gives fabs a secondary supply of China-concentrated tungsten and scarce hafnium and ruthenium.

title: Regenerative braking for wordlines: charge recycling between successive row activations
idea: EVs and elevators recover braking energy instead of burning it as heat. Inside the die, when a row is precharged its ~3 V wordline dumps charge into a local reservoir capacitor that then pre-charges the next activated wordline and feeds the VPP pump, recovering ~40-50% of wordline CV^2 energy; commands and timings at the DDR/HBM pins are unchanged.
why: Fact 10: the ~3 V wordline locks CV^2 energy; recycling cuts activate energy and VPP charge-pump power and area, lowering energy per bit without a new interface.

title: Resonant-tunneling Goto-pair latch built from silicon and oxide only
idea: Effect: negative differential resistance in two series Si/SiO2 (or Si/CaF2) double-barrier resonant-tunneling diodes makes a bistable midpoint node (Goto pair) that holds a bit at nA standby with no capacitor. One access transistor completes a ~3-device static cell, with no III-V and no Ge.
why: Capacitor elimination and refresh-free operation; the cell is ~2-3x DRAM area but needs no high-AR capacitor etch or high-k, so tool capital per wafer drops.

title: Anodic-alumina self-ordered pores replace lithography for vertical-channel stacks
idea: Ideal: a memory array that grows itself in a beaker. Closest: atop a Mo/SiO2 tier stack, anodize a Masuda-pre-textured aluminum film into perfectly ordered hexagonal pores (~40 nm pitch) used as a litho-free, self-aligned mask for the vertical holes; ALD ZnSnO channels make strings of 64-128 volatile gain cells, with bitlines registered to the AAO lattice rows.
why: 100x: array cell definition costs one wet anodization (~$0.1/m2) instead of EUV multipatterning; ~7e10 sites/cm2 x 100 tiers ~ 0.9 TB/cm2 raw, so even 5% array efficiency reaches ~$0.05-0.1/GB. Trades pore-domain defects (spare mapping) and us-class string latency hidden by caching.

title: Substitute anodized aluminum pores for EUV-patterned capacitor holes
idea: Deposit a thick Al film over the cell array and anodize it in oxalic or phosphoric acid from an imprinted seed-pit pattern so self-ordered hexagonal pores grow straight down at 100-300:1 aspect ratio; line the pores with TiN/high-k/TiN and keep the alumina as a rigid mold that prevents leaning.
why: Replaces 1-2 EUV exposures and the fluorocarbon high-AR etch with room-temperature electrochemistry; AR >115 becomes cheap, breaking the charge wall. Aluminum is abundant and US-smelted.

title: Trusted-foundry molybdenum wordlines from Colorado ore replace Chinese tungsten
idea: Defense trusted-foundry users must avoid adversary-sourced metals. Molybdenum is mined in the U.S. (Climax, Henderson) and has a shorter electron mean free path than W, so it beats W resistivity in <20 nm trenches. Deposit Mo by ALD/CVD from MoO2Cl2 into buried wordlines and bit-line contacts with thin or no TiN liner.
why: Removes ~80%-China tungsten and WF6 from the cell array and lowers wordline RC ~20-30% thanks to liner-less fill.

title: Anodized-alumina pores as self-ordered capacitor holes, no plasma etch
idea: Revive 1960s anodized thin-film capacitor chemistry: anodize an aluminum layer over the transistor array so self-ordered hexagonal pores (40 nm pitch, aspect ratio 100+:1) grow without lithography or plasma etch. The pores are lined with ALD TiN/Al2O3-TiO2/TiN, and each DUV-defined landing pad collects several pores in parallel.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1) with no EUV, no PFAS high-aspect-ratio etch (the costliest DRAM etch) and no Hf, using a water-based oxalic acid electrolyte; claims aspect ratio >100 at near-zero etch cost.

title: Bamboo: NiAl intermetallic bamboo-grain wordlines from abundant metals
idea: Stimulus 'bamboo' (nodes span the full stalk width) -> deposit B2-NiAl into buried-wordline trenches so single grains span the line (bamboo grains), exploiting NiAl's short electron mean free path (~5 nm) so resistivity barely rises at 10 nm widths, and its ~1,640 C melting point to survive the DRAM thermal budget.
why: Replaces tungsten with nickel plus aluminum; at sub-15 nm widths effective resistivity can match or beat W, lowering wordline RC and drive energy.

title: Counter-current rinse cascade: last rinse feeds the first
idea: Reverse water flow direction: the cleanest final-rinse water flows backward to feed earlier, dirtier rinse stages and then pre-wash, as in counter-current extraction, before reclaim.
why: Ultrapure water use per wafer down ~3-5x, which helps U.S. siting where water is the gate.

title: Atanasoff capacitor-drum regeneration on Gen-10.5 display glass panels
idea: Revive the 1942 Atanasoff-Berry 'jogged' capacitor memory as huge-area arrays on 3 m display glass: LTPS TFTs and metal-insulator-metal capacitors at 1.5 um design rules, with ABC-style continuous regeneration by row-parallel sense circuits at the panel edge.
why: No EUV, no Czochralski wafers or quartz crucibles (glass is made from sand), and it reuses idle panel fabs; ~9 m2 per substrate offsets the low density; claims 5-10x lower capex per bit for bulk, slower tiers.

title: Gen-10.5 display-glass panels stacked with twenty tiers of oxide-TFT DRAM
idea: Ideal: memory sold like window glass. Closest: use Gen-10.5 display lines (~9.9 m2 panels) to build 2T0C/1T1C tiers from In-free ZnSnO TFTs, Mo/Al lines and planar Al2O3/TiO2 caps (TFT off-current ~1e-21 A/um makes small caps adequate), 4-5 masks per tier with panel nanoimprint at F~0.25 um, 20 tiers stacked at <=350 C.
why: 100x: panel processing ~$25/m2 per tier vs ~$150k/m2 for leading DRAM wafers; at ~0.5 um2/bit (~250 GB/m2/tier) x 20 tiers = 5 TB/m2 for ~$500 -> ~$0.1/GB vs ~$10/GB today. Trades latency (100-300 ns), volume and power; zero EUV, W, Hf, He.

title: Holtronic's lesson: Talbot self-imaging prints sub-micron memory arrays on panels
idea: Holtronic's total-internal-reflection holographic lithography died needing perfectly flat substrates and costly holograms for arbitrary patterns. Memory arrays are periodic: displacement Talbot lithography (a grating mask lit by collimated i-line light while the gap scans one Talbot period) prints focus-insensitive 200-400 nm hole and line arrays across warped Gen-8 glass, with ordinary panel steppers only for periphery.
why: Raises glass-panel memory density ~10-30x over 1.2 um panel steppers with no EUV or projection optics; the mask is a cheap grating; lamp energy only; fluorine-free i-line resists.

title: Molten-salt electro-deoxidation turns ordinary sand into domestic silicon feedstock
idea: Effect: field-driven oxide-ion migration. In the FFC-Cambridge process O2- ions leave a SiO2 cathode into molten CaCl2 at ~850 C, leaving porous silicon with no carbothermic arc furnace or chlorosilane Siemens reactor; directional solidification and segregation refining then push purity toward CZ feedstock grade.
why: Polysilicon concentration (China ~90%) and Siemens energy (~50-60 kWh/kg): targets <20 kWh/kg from any sand at U.S. sites.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching revives the deep silicon trench capacitor
idea: Combine catalytic metal-assisted chemical etching (Ag nanodots sinking through Si in HF/H2O2) with the old trench-DRAM capacitor: block-copolymer-placed dots carve 15 nm holes at >200:1 aspect ratio in silicon, catalyst is stripped in HNO3, then ALD ZrO2/TiN lines the holes.
why: Goes far past the 60-75:1 plasma-etch limit without fluorocarbon gases or plasma etch tools; Cs >10 fF; capital for the hardest etch drops ~10x.

title: Pharmaceutical cyclic-olefin polymers replace fluoropolymer wetted parts
idea: Pharma prefilled syringes use cyclic olefin polymer (COP/COC) because it has extremely low leachables. Adapt COP-lined, PEEK-bodied valves, filters and distribution lines for UPW and non-oxidizing dilute acids in place of PFA/PVDF, keeping fluoropolymer only for ozone, peroxide and solvent service.
why: Fluoropolymer piping is a PFAS regulatory risk and a concentrated supply. UPW loops are the largest wetted surface in a fab, so converting them roughly halves fluoropolymer mass.

title: Transient-implant chemistry: cleavable-crosslink underfill frees good dies from bad stacks
idea: Biodegradable implant electronics are designed to come apart on cue. Formulate stack underfill and mold compound with acid-cleavable acetal/ketal crosslinks that survive reflow but dissolve in a mild acid bath, so a stack with one bad die is taken apart and its good dies are re-stacked. Test bond strength, warpage and debond in a university packaging lab.
why: HBM stack yield loss (fact 6: 20-30%) throws away fully processed good dies; reclaiming them cuts wafer starts and all materials per good stack ~10-20%.

title: Sliding ferroelectric boron nitride bilayers: switch by gliding, not ions
idea: Inverts 'polarization switching means displacing ions, which fatigues': store the bit in the stacking order (AB vs BA) of a bilayer hexagonal boron nitride, flipped by a vertical field that slides the layers one bond length; sliding creates no vacancies, so endurance may be effectively unlimited.
why: Nonvolatile, zero refresh; atomically thin cell made of boron and nitrogen only, with no Hf, W or PFAS chemistry.

title: Mushroom-body sparse wide access hides slow printed cells
idea: Insect mushroom bodies get fast recall from ~200k slow Kenyon cells through sparse, very wide parallel coding. Organize printed memory sheets as 64k-bit-wide rows read at once into an on-silicon SRAM landing buffer with prefetch, so ~1 us printed cells supply the bandwidth while the SRAM serves 10-100 ns hits.
why: This architecture lets abundant printed memory do DRAM's job for streaming and AI-weight workloads without fab capital, EUV or Cz wafers.

title: Supercritical CO2 rinsing eliminates surface tension and ultrapure water
idea: Effect: above its critical point (31 C, 74 bar) CO2 has zero surface tension and liquid-like solvating power. Post-etch residue removal and drying of 70:1 capacitor pillars runs in recycled sCO2 with a cosolvent instead of UPW rinse and IPA dry, so capillary forces cannot collapse the pillars.
why: Water intensity (several m3 UPW per wafer) and the pillar-collapse limit on capacitor aspect ratio (fact 1), allowing taller capacitors.

title: Salt shaker: molten-salt electrolysis turns sand into domestic polysilicon
idea: Stimulus 'salt' -> reduce high-purity SiO2 pellets directly to silicon as the cathode in molten CaCl2 at ~850 C (FFC-Cambridge style), skipping carbothermic smelting and the trichlorosilane Siemens process, then zone-refine to electronic grade.
why: Polysilicon is >80% China-concentrated and Siemens costs ~50-60 kWh/kg; electrolysis could roughly halve energy and allow small modular U.S. plants.

title: Turn polysilicon-plant waste SiCl4 into synthetic-silica crucibles
idea: Ideal: crucibles made from something we throw away. Closest: route silicon tetrachloride byproduct from U.S. Siemens-process polysilicon plants through flame hydrolysis into synthetic fused-silica soot, then sinter into full-body or inner-wall crucibles with ~10x lower metal impurities than natural HPQ.
why: Swaps the Spruce Pine HPQ chokepoint for a domestic waste stream (~3 t SiCl4 per t of poly already exists) and closes the chlorine loop.
